overview.description: Flow cytometry measures thousands of single cells per second by light scatter and fluorescence, and FACS sorts them. It is the standard tool for immunophenotyping, viability, and screening engineered cells - and demands careful controls and compensation.
objectives: interpret forward scatter (size) and side scatter (granularity)
gate populations and use FMO / unstained controls
compensate for spectral overlap between fluorophores
design a panel and sort target cells by FACS

steps.description: Flow cytometry measures thousands of single cells per second by light scatter and fluorescence, and FACS sorts them. It is the standard tool for immunophenotyping, viability, and screening engineered cells - and demands careful controls and compensation.
steps.intro: Flow data is only as good as its controls: without compensation and proper gating, spectral spillover and debris masquerade as real populations.

instructions.title: Prep a single-cell suspension
instructions.description: Dissociate and filter to avoid clumps; stain with fluorophore-conjugated markers or use a fluorescent reporter.

instructions.title: Set scatter gates
instructions.description: Use FSC/SSC to gate cells vs debris and singlets vs doublets before looking at fluorescence.

instructions.title: Compensate
instructions.description: Use single-stain controls to correct spectral overlap; use FMO controls to set positive/negative boundaries.

instructions.title: Analyse or sort
instructions.description: Quantify populations, or physically sort target cells by FACS for downstream culture/analysis.

submission.description: Design a small flow panel with the controls (unstained, single-stain, FMO) needed to gate and compensate it correctly, and explain what each control rules out.

kits.name: Core-facility / community-lab access
kits.note: Flow cytometers are institutional; book time at a university core or community lab.

kits.name: Fluorescence microscope (proxy)
kits.note: See labelled cells and gating intuition at the bench before a real cytometer.
